title: Add deterministic fallback/runbook requirements and acceptance tests to runtime PRD
creator: Monica Alvarez
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-01-28 production incident (postmortem link below) autoscaler thrash combined with a broad fallback to CPU-backed instances led to a prolonged period of elevated P95 latency and token cost spikes for several customers. The postmortem called out two categories of gaps: (1) PRD requirements that do not specify deterministic fallback eligibility and rollback criteria, and (2) absence of automated acceptance tests and load-sim artifacts to validate fallback behavior before rollout.

Goal:
Update the runtime PRD to translate the postmortem action items into clear product requirements: a fallback/failover matrix, explicit SLO degradation thresholds that trigger automated vs. manual actions, a standardized runbook template, and a set of automated acceptance tests (load + regression) that must pass before any rollout that touches routing, autoscaling, or fallback logic.

Scope (what will change in PRD):
- Add a "Fallback behavior and rollback" section with a machine-readable matrix describing: trigger signals, priority order of fallback targets (model variant, region, capacity tier, CPU fallback), time-to-rollback, and cost/quality trade-offs.
- Define SLO degradation thresholds to classify incidents (green/yellow/red) and tie those to allowed automatic actions (e.g., cache-only fallback allowed in yellow; full model downgrade requires manual approval).
- Require instrumentation/telemetry hooks: explicit metrics for fallback count, fallback duration, affected-tokens, and quality-regression indicators (e.g., rerank delta, hallucination rate proxy).
- Mandate an automated acceptance test harness for fallback scenarios: reproducible load profiles, failure injection knobs, and post-test regression checks. Tests must be runnable in a dedicated staging environment and gated in the rollout pipeline.
- Introduce a runbook template as a PRD appendix: roles, escalation path, rollback checklist, post-incident communications, and customer notification windows.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Implementing the autoscaler algorithm changes (ENG tickets will own).
- Full retrospective on every previously impacted customer (customer success will follow up separately).

Acceptance criteria (high level) - see list field below for specific pass/fail criteria.

Artifacts and links:

- Current runtime PRD (to be updated): https://confluence.redwood.ai/prds/runtime-prd-v1.19
- Draft runbook template (engineering draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/runbook-template.md
- Load test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fallback-test-harness/pulls/34
- Dashboard to monitor fallback metrics: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/fallback-metrics

Notes on trade-offs and decisions so far (timeline):
- 2026-02-12: Triage meeting — decided we must add deterministic acceptance tests to PRD before next major runtime release.
- 2026-02-18: Engineering feasibility sync — ENG estimated 3-4 sprints for test harness hardening; agreed PRD can require tests runnable in staging with synthetic profiles.
- 2026-02-24: Product/Legal flagged customer-notification windows; legal asked that the PRD include maximum notification lead times for planned fallbacks that could affect SLAs.
- 2026-02-28: Design review — console messaging patterns approved; need copy revisions for cascading fallback warnings.
- 2026-03-01: PM drafted acceptance criteria and added owner matrix.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains a fallback matrix that enumerates triggers, targets, and time-to-rollback for at least three classes of failure (network/globally-degraded, autoscaler-thrash, model-quality-regression)
SLO degradation thresholds are defined (numeric thresholds for P50/P95/P99 latency, 5xx rate, and token-cost-per-second) and mapped to allowed actions (automatic, semi-automatic, manual)
Telemetry contract added: metrics, tags, and dashboards required for any fallback change (fallback_count, fallback_duration_ms, affected_customers, quality_regression_score)

Automated acceptance test harness described in PRD and linked: tests can run in a staging environment and include failure injection and regression assertions; passing tests required for rollout gating
Runbook template appended to PRD and reviewed by SRE, with clear escalation and rollback checklists
Console messages and customer notification windows defined and validated by Design and Legal
Ownership matrix included with primary and secondary owners for fallback behavior, runbook maintenance, and test harness upkeep
